On Tue, Jun 30, 2026 at 09:25 AM Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com> wrote:
> Sean / Marissa — looping you in for urgent triage and customer comms.

I dug into the logs and infra telemetry. Short summary: at 03:14:03 UTC we completed a kernel-selector rollout that changed the default preference to the new quantized int8 kernel set (label: int8-agg-v2) for many medium-length sequence profiles. Two side-effects we're seeing:

1) The new selector increases micro-batching to improve throughput for some profiles but interacts poorly with our KV-cache hot-path. For chat workloads with many short prefix tokens and frequent KV cache reuse, this increases per-token overhead and reduces observed TPS.
2) The int8 execution path has an unexpected branch that triggers a fallback path for certain attention kernel sizes, causing a CPU-side copy/transform on each generation step — this inflates latency at p95/p99.

I've opened Ops incident OPS-INC-2026-2394 and attached a set of flamegraphs + kernel traces (ops_flamegraphs.tar.gz). Early numbers: after selector flip, aggregate TPS for Acme's fleet dropped ~45% and p99 increased ~3x for sequences in the 160–400 token range.

Mitigation proposal (recommended order):
- Immediate: roll back kernel-selector default to previous profile v1 for affected pools (we can do this per-customer pool).
- Short term: enable a runtime heuristic to prefer non-quantized kernel when sequence length and KV reuse exceed thresholds.
- Postmortem: audit kernel selector tests and add a regression eval with Acme's prompt set.

I'm standing by to execute rollback; will need thumbs from Product/AE for customer-facing comms.

— Sean (oncall SRE)

Subject: Resolved: root cause & next steps for ACME outage this morning

Sara — thanks again for the quick report and for your patience. Summary and next steps below: 

What happened (short):
- A kernel-selector rollout shifted many medium-length seqs to a new int8-quantized kernel path (int8-agg-v2). For workloads with heavy KV-cache reuse (typical of your chat prefixes) this caused unexpected per-token CPU copy/transform overhead and reduced effective TPS; in some cases it triggered a fallback path that drove p99 higher.

Immediate action taken:
- Rolled back the selector for Acme's pool (rbk-20260630-01). Post-rollback metrics show TPS and p95/p99 back near baseline (see post_rollback_metrics.csv).

Root cause and mitigation plan:
1) Root cause: insufficient regression coverage for the selector change on KV-cache-heavy prompt shapes — the int8 path had a performance cliff for certain kernel sizes.
2) Short-term mitigation: we will canary an adjusted selector with a runtime heuristic to prefer the non-quantized path when KV reuse and sequence length thresholds are met.
3) Long-term: add Acme's prompt set to our selector/regression suite, expand perf tests to include KV-reuse scenarios, and harden the rollback/runbook steps.

We will follow up with a formal postmortem (OPS-INC-2026-2394) and share timing for the canary. If you prefer, we can schedule a joint 30-minute postmortem call to walk through the tech details.

Again, apologies for the disruption — we appreciate the callout and will work to prevent this in future deployments.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
